Version packages (#50)

This PR was opened by the [Changesets
release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When
you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will
be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release
yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will
be updated.


# Releases
## openfilm@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - `openfilm capture <url>
<file.png>` takes a picture of a live web page in the browser OpenFilm
draws films in, with nothing to install: a product or a site shown as it
is, sharp enough to fill the stage. It can take the whole page, one
element, a phone-sized window or the dark theme, and click or hide
things first.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - An official skill,
`replicate`: give the agent a video and it makes yours like it, keeping
its structure, rhythm, look and motion while the content is yours. It
watches the reference whole and in stretches with `openfilm look`,
starts from an example's source when one fits, writes a plan part by
part, and compares the two side by side. It never reuses the reference's
footage, music, voice or words.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Saved: your own
library, the same in every project. The bookmark button beside Upload
switches the media pane to it, and back; it is the same pane, so upload,
folders, list and grid, filters, sort, search, rename, move and delete
all work there, and anything can go in it: video, pictures, sound,
documents, any file. Right-click a clip on the timeline or the picture,
or a file of the project, and choose Add to Saved; with several clips
selected, save them as one (they come back on tracks of their own, laid
out as they were, links kept) or each alone. Drag anything from Saved
onto the timeline, or press Enter: a file is imported into the project
as one from your computer is, and a saved clip comes back as you saved
it, with its place, its look and the changes made in its page, its files
copied into the project, so changing it there never changes the saved
one. Saved is a folder beside your projects (Movies/OpenFilm/Saved on a
Mac), so you can also add to it from Finder. The media pane no longer
has a close button: the assets button beside the chat opens and closes
it.

Template: select a page clip and the inspector shows what its page lets
you change, without opening the page: each of its words, each of its
pictures (replace one with a picture of the project, one dropped from
the media pane, or one from your computer), and the CSS custom
properties its stylesheet sets on `:root` (a color with a color picker,
a number with its unit, a font with the font picker, words in quotes as
text). Each change is kept for that clip only, and one changed can go
back to the page's own. A page saved with such properties is marked as a
template in Saved.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Nine more official
skills, each with a version, so you can tell which one made a film:

- Workflows: `long-to-short` (a long video cut into shorts that stand
alone), `screen-demo` (a screen recording made into a polished demo),
`motion-graphics` (studio-level motion graphics), `presenter-pip` (you
speaking from a small window while the content fills the screen).
- Styles: `whiteboard` (drawn by hand as a voice explains),
`vintage-film` (photos as old film and instant prints), `lyric-video` (a
song's lyrics as the picture, every word on the voice), `keynote` (a
launch film with your real product on stage), `collage` (cut-paper
motion graphics).

A skill's openfilm.json can now give its `version`, its `kind`
(`workflow` or `style`), its `order`, an `icon`, a `cover` picture and a
`preview` video.

The Community's skills are redesigned: a row of filters at the top (all,
yours, this project's, workflows, styles) with adding a skill beside it;
yours come first; a note on what skills are for; and a skill opens as a
page with its picture or preview on the left and what it is, its version
and using it on the right.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Tabs: the desktop
window keeps each open project in a tab of its own, in Studio's top bar,
side by side, the one in front in the panes' color. `+` (⌘T) opens the
projects window, and the project picked opens in a new tab (or comes
forward, when it is open already). ⌘W closes a tab, ⇧⌘T opens the last
one closed again, ⌘1–9 and ⌃Tab switch. A tab shows when an agent is
working in it, when one is waiting for your answer, and an export's
progress; agents and exports go on in tabs behind. The tabs come back as
you left them; with none open, the window shows your projects. The
projects window has two views: your projects, and Examples, where
example films play their preview under the pointer and open on a page of
their own with their parts, to start a new film from. Skills show their
own title and summary in your language (a skill's optional
`openfilm.json`). An examples index can list each example's `category`,
`segments` and a `video` preview; one read from a file has its pictures
served by Studio. Studio in a browser keeps its projects window, now
with the same two views.

### Patch Changes

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - In OpenFilm an agent
keeps its maker's own MCP servers, but the ones you added to it yourself
stay off until you turn each on. The switches are in Settings → Agents,
under the agent; this covers Claude Code (its claude.ai connectors
stay), Codex, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI and Copilot. Your own
skills now stay off in Qwen Code and Gemini CLI too, and Copilot and
Qwen Code get OpenFilm's skills. Claude Code's skill filter no longer
waits for a first session to learn its skills.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - `openfilm get asr` now
keeps the transcript beside any recording in the project, not only those
under `assets/`. A file at the top of the project, or a reference video
in `references/`, gets its WebVTT too. Before, none was kept and the
answer wrongly said the service does not time words. In Studio, making
subtitles now works for a clip whose file is outside `assets/`: before,
it was transcribed on every try and nothing was kept. Files and folders
starting with a dot (`.git`) belong to the tools, so a recording there
is refused before anything is sent.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - When the preview can't
be drawn in Safari or Firefox, Studio now says why: films are drawn and
exported with Chromium, so a page may use something that browser doesn't
have, and Chrome or Edge shows it. The README says which browsers to
open Studio in.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio: a click on the
picture takes what is under a full-frame overlay. When the clip on top
has nothing there but a layer filling its page (a letterbox, a vignette,
grain laid over the film), the click, the hover outline and a
double-click to type go to the title or picture under it in the clip
below. Before, the overlay's clip was taken and nothing under it could
be picked in the picture.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: when Codex is
installed more than once, as a command installed long ago and the copy
inside the Codex or ChatGPT app (or a Microsoft Store app), the newer
one is used: the models Codex offers depend on its version, so an old
copy showed only a few. On Windows, a reason Codex could not start is
readable instead of `������` on a system in Chinese or another
non-English language.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: when Codex is
found but can't start, the chat's model menu now says why, in Codex's
own words, instead of only "Couldn't start it to read its settings". A
Codex older than the chat needs says to update it. Settings → Agents no
longer shows Codex as connected when it can't read its own config file,
and names the setting it could not read.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: a file added
to the message you are writing opens to look at, as one in a sent
message does: click a video to play it, a picture to see it large, a
text to read it.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: the files
added to the message you are writing show in whole rows, up to three at
once, so a message's twelve files are all in view. Before, the second
row was cut in half and had to be scrolled to.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio's preview no
longer flashes at a cut. A page coming on used to show before its frame
was drawn, so for a moment it showed how it looked before: its first
state, or the frame it drew the last time it was on. Now it shows once
that frame is drawn, and the picture before it stays until then. Exports
were never affected.

- [#47](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/47)
[`e70d9d9`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/e70d9d93c7bebe3d634ff2caa6f7a738cdde59d3)
Thanks [@wang135531](https://github.com/wang135531)! - Speech
recognition with Doubao using your Volcengine Speech API key, with
word-timed transcripts from audio and video recordings.

Keep transcript lines visible through their timed words, even when
speech is slower than the estimated reading time.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - The Examples and the
skills show at once. OpenFilm comes with a copy of the examples index
and its posters, and keeps the last index it read, so the Examples tab
no longer waits on GitHub (a slow or blocked connection showed nothing);
the newest index is read in the background as Studio starts. A gallery
opened again shows what it read before while it asks again, skill covers
and example posters stay in the browser's cache, and the app reads what
the composer's skills need as it starts.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio: words typed
into a line in the picture show in the inspector as they are typed. Its
text box and the layer's name follow each key, and go back to the old
words when the edit is given up with Esc. Before, the inspector kept the
old words until Enter.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: Your own key
works again. The 0.1.7 installer carried newer versions of the agent's
packages than the ones tested, one of which no longer fit, so every
message ended with "ACP connection closed". The installer now carries
exactly the versions in the lockfile, and its build stops if any differ.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Settings → Agents: an
agent that is connected shows Disconnect alone. Locate… is offered when
it is disconnected (beside Connect) or not found.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio: a theme change
reaches everything at once. The audio meters beside the timeline and the
clips' waveforms are drawn again in the new theme's colors (before, they
kept the other theme's, such as dark meter bars in the light theme,
until the film played), and every other open page of Studio, such as
another tab of the app, takes the theme too.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - A film with hundreds of
sounds renders and exports on Windows. Its mix no longer puts everything
on one command line, which Windows limits to 32,767 characters: a sound
used by many clips is read once, and a long mix's graph goes in a file.

- [#53](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/53)
[`b138595`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/b138595d4c2d1fa5262b4a8a8c7cd98187c4b077)
Thanks [@HEOJUNFO](https://github.com/HEOJUNFO)! - A timecode typed into
the inspector at 23.976, 29.97 or 59.94 fps lands on the frame that
shows that timecode, instead of the frame before it, and a typed `12f`
counts frames at the real rate.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Your own key's agent
gets a shorter system prompt with no conflicting instructions. It was
told both that it already had the manual and that it should print it,
and both to open Studio and never to open it. Rules it got two or three
times are now said once. Its own part is a third shorter, and the manual
is unchanged.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: Your own key
is an agent with models of your own, each set up on its own: the name
the chat shows, the API format and address of its service, its own key,
the model asked for there, and the reasoning efforts it takes. The
chat's model menu switches between them, from one service to another, as
it does for the other agents. A model on an address already set up can
take that model's key. Models set up before become one each, on the
service and key they had.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Settings: Models is now
Services (which service makes each kind of media), and your own services
moved there as Custom services. One is set up with its name, address,
key and a description of what it does and how it is called (or where its
API docs are): where the key goes is no longer asked, since your agent
puts it where the service's docs say.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Settings say what is
there now: Custom services take as many services as you like, and say
you can also tell your agent about a service in the chat (one with a key
is better set up there, so the key stays out of the conversation). The
note pointing to the old "Your own services" is gone, Agents describes
your own key as models you set up, Providers says the choice of each
kind of media is under Services, and the sign-in wait no longer names
Terminal (Windows opens PowerShell).

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Skills: ways of making
a kind of film, each a folder with a SKILL.md and the files it brings.
`openfilm skills` lists the skills a film can be made with: the
project's own (in its `skills/` folder), yours (in
`~/Movies/OpenFilm/Skills`), and the official ones. `openfilm skill
<name>` prints one for the agent to follow. `openfilm skill add <GitHub
address or folder>` adds a skill to yours and lists any scripts it
brings. The manual tells agents about them. Studio no longer lists pages
inside a project's `skills/` folder.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - In the chat, a skill
can be named in a message: type `/`, or pick one in the Community; it
goes in as a pill and the agent gets the skill's instructions with the
message. The composer's Community button opens over your film on the
skills (official, yours, this project's), with the examples beside them:
point the agent at an example, or a part of one (a segment, or a stretch
dragged on its strip), and it reads how that film is made; or start a
new film from it, in a tab of its own. Add a skill there from a GitHub
link or a folder, or make one with the agent. In OpenFilm an agent keeps
its maker's own skills and gets OpenFilm's, but the skills you installed
in it yourself stay off until you turn each on in Settings → Agents.
This works for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and your own key's agent;
agents that can't be told say they use all of yours. The context ring is
gone: when a conversation is nearly full, a line above the composer
offers a new one.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Your own skills are
kept in `~/Movies/OpenFilm/Skills` (beside Projects and Exports, backed
up with them); skills kept in `~/.openfilm/skills` move there on their
own. A skill replaced or removed goes to the trash, never deleted, and
`openfilm skill remove <name>` moves one there. Adding from a link or a
folder shows what came first: each skill, its size, the scripts it
brings and any of yours it would replace, then Add or Cancel. The
switches for an agent's own skills are in Settings → Agents, beside its
MCP servers. OpenFilm's own skill for terminal agents is no longer shown
in the app.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio: a project with
thousands of files plays smoothly as soon as it opens. While its files'
lengths and sizes were read, each answer laid out the media pane again
(tens of ms with that many files), so the picture stalled again and
again for the first minutes. The answers now come in a few times a
second, and the pane works out its folders in one pass.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Desktop: stopping the
agent while a command it ran was still going no longer starts a turn of
its own a moment later, "A background task finished; the agent went on",
that Stop could not end. The rest of a command from a turn that already
ended (its last output, its exit) now stays out of the chat. Stop ends a
turn the agent started by itself at once. Such a turn that ends with
nothing in it leaves no line behind, including ones already saved.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Choose where new
projects go. Settings → General → Storage shows the folder, with the
free space on its disk, and lets you change it (or go back to the
default), for example to keep large projects off a full system disk.
Exports go where you pick when exporting, as before. New projects,
including ones fetched with `openfilm open`, go to the folder you
choose; projects made before stay where they are and still open from the
list. On Windows, the installer now asks where to install the app.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio: a short clip's
thumbnails fill it. Each picture in a clip's row was squeezed to the
clip's width while the pictures kept their places, so the clip's color
showed between them and the row looked broken.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - A turn's log (Settings
→ Developer) now shows everything the agent and its model got. A new
"Sent to the agent" tab shows how the app started the agent, every word
it adds to the agent's own instructions, and each message exactly as the
agent got it, with its pictures. Model requests are no longer only your
own key's: for Claude Code, Codex and Kimi they are read from each
agent's own record. Each request shows its full system prompt, its
tools, every message (including what the agent added by itself: project
instructions, environment, skill lists, reminders), the answer and its
tokens. Subagents' requests are included. Turns from before this change
show their requests too, as long as the agent's record is still there.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - A turn's log (Settings
→ Developer) now shows model requests for Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot,
Qwen Code, CodeBuddy and OpenCode too: each request's system prompt,
tools, every message (including what the agent added by itself), the
answer and its tokens. With Developer mode on, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code,
CodeBuddy and OpenCode are started with their own local logging switch,
written into a folder of the app's and kept for a week. The app leaves
any telemetry you set yourself as it is. CodeBuddy is logged only when
its own telemetry is off (`DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`), since otherwise its
traces would name each logged file. Copilot's requests are rebuilt from
its own record, which has no tool definitions. Where a log lacks
something, the viewer says so, and it explains a turn that has no
requests (Cursor makes its prompt on its servers).

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - A turn's log shows how
the session's skills and MCP servers were set: OpenFilm's skills, your
own skills and servers kept off, and the ones you let in. A thought the
agent did not keep in its record now says so, instead of showing 0
characters.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Studio run with npm
updates itself: when a newer OpenFilm is out, Update appears in the top
bar (and in Settings → About), and a click runs the newest in the
background; Studio starts again on it and the page comes back on the new
version. `openfilm update` does the same from a terminal, or for an
agent asked to update OpenFilm. The desktop app's Studio still updates
with the app.

- [#58](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/58)
[`8ca326c`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/8ca326c24970fd6f639b3af064a0ea298ff2bdf6)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - What's new: 0.1.7's
